Tide Pools of the Pacific

Tide pools form where the ocean leaves water behind in rocky basins at low tide. They host anemones, sea stars, hermit crabs, and small fish that tolerate rapid changes in temperature and salinity across a single day.

The best time to visit is during a negative tide, when the water line drops below the average low. Check the tide tables before you go, and read the tide pool etiquette guide to avoid harming the animals.

What lives there

  • Ochre sea stars, which cling to rocks with hundreds of tube feet.
  • Giant green anemones, whose colour comes from symbiotic algae.
  • Hermit crabs that trade shells as they grow larger.

Each zone of the shore has its own community, from the splash zone that only waves reach to the low zone that is uncovered just a few times a month. Animals in the high zone endure the longest exposure to air and sun.
